evidence: Three top-level packages (scratch, first-edition/code, first-edition/code-python3) suggest logical grouping without strict inter-package dependencies
All code resides in a single repository with no external service boundaries or network communication patterns
High average fan-out (4.5) indicates modules depend on many other internal modules, typical of tightly integrated monoliths
Directory depth is shallow (max 3), suggesting flat, logical modularity rather than deep hierarchical distribution
Code modules are organized by domain (e.g., clustering.py, linear_algebra.py, neural_networks.py) with clear responsibilities but cross-module imports
No evidence of ports/adapters separators, event buses, or API-gateway-like patterns
All modules use local imports (e.g., from scratch.linear_algebra import Vector), confirming colocated execution
Architectural factors C1, C2, A3 (likely cohesion, compartmentalization, and abstraction) and maintainability factors T4 (testability), A1 (adaptability) align with modular monolith traits
risks: Tight coupling between modules may reduce testability and reusability
Shared execution context makes horizontal scaling impossible without repartitioning
Domain bleed may occur as no strict boundary enforcement (e.g., no hexagonal ports) exists
Growing codebase may eventually exceed maintainability limits of single deployment unit
